### 2026-10-17 – This session I designed the Bible of the lock (the part that the core goes into) and the Bible cover. I had some issues designing the Bible cover because I wasn't exactly sour how I wanted it to inter

**2h**

This session I designed the Bible of the lock (the part that the core goes into) and the Bible cover. I had some issues designing the Bible cover because I wasn't exactly sour how I wanted it to interact with the Bible, but I'm pretty happy with the solution I ended up on because it's pretty simple and should be reliable and easy to assemble. I was also playing around with the assembly feature for a while to try to get the lock moving like it's supposed to, and I'm really enjoying seeing it all come together. Also, I've decided that I won't be making a whole padlock because 3d modeling is taking a lot longer then expected. I'm just going to design a KIK cylinder instead, so it will still be a working lock just smaller and with less parts.

### 2026-10-18 – This afternoon I had a VERY long session. I needed to get this project done before the deadline tonight, and I somehow finished it.

**7h**

This afternoon I had a VERY long session. I needed to get this project done before the deadline tonight, and I somehow finished it.

I started out by doing some more 3d modeling. I'm still not great at it, but I can tell that I'm getting better. I modified the plug to hold a C-clip, and then modeled the C-clip itself. After this I modeled the driver pin and 7 different lengths of Key pin for the lock. After joining all of these together in an assembly, I finished the model!

With this project, I wanted to be able to generate any key that I wanted, so with a little help from ai, I was able to create a script that can generate a key from a given key code, so that why anyone who prints the lock can have their own unique key. This was a LOT more complicated than I though, and took over half of this session to finish. I ended up needing 16 variations of the script to get it right, but I'm pretty satisfied with the final product!

After this, I added some stuff to the Github and wrote the README as well as making the Bill of Materials.
